served as `favoriteCount`, and `createdAt/updatedAt` as `created/updated`.

filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` — the article ids are being compared to author ids. Even
once the `favorites` relation is loaded, the result is wrong.

**Rule:** when a filter is "articles in this set", the column is `article.id`. Read the
`andWhere` literally; do not trust the variable name.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > What it is
A backend implementing the [RealWorld](https://github.com/gothinkster/realworld) API spec
(Medium clone: users, profiles, articles, comments, tags, favourites, follows). Any RealWorld
frontend (React, Vue, Angular…) is expected to work against it unchanged — **spec conformance
is the contract**, not just "it works with our own client".

Pinned at upstream commit `c1c2cc4` of `lujakob/nestjs-realworld-example-app` (2021-01-18).

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Every handler returns the RO envelope, never a bare entity (#57)
**What happened:** `ArticleController.create()` returned `ArticleEntity` directly while every
other handler returns `{ article }`. The React frontend read `response.article.slug` → `Cannot
read property 'slug' of undefined` right after creating an article. The server logged nothing —
from its side the request succeeded.

**Rule:** the envelope (`ArticleRO`, `UserRO`, …) is the contract with every RealWorld client.
A handler whose return type is not a `*RO` interface is a bug even if it "works" in Postman.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls
`user.favorites.findIndex(...)`. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany`, so it is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on
`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

**Rule:** a `simple-array` filter needs delimiter-aware matching (e.g. compare against

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

| Module | Guarded routes (401 without token) |
|---|---|
| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |
| `ArticleModule` | `GET /articles/feed` · `POST /articles` · `PUT /articles/:slug` · `DELETE /articles/:slug` · `POST /articles/:slug/comments` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` · `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` |

`ArticleService.slugify()` = `slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + <6 base-36 chars from Math.random()>`.

`RO` means **Response Object**. Every controller method returns the RealWorld envelope, named
`<Thing>RO` in `*.interface.ts`:

| Endpoint family | Returns | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| single article | `ArticleRO` | `{ article: {...} }` |
| list | `ArticlesRO` | `{ articles: [...], articlesCount: n }` |
| comments | `CommentsRO` | `{ comments: [...] }` |
| user | `UserRO` | `{ user: {..., token} }` |
| profile | `ProfileRO` | `{ profile: {..., following} }` |

bare entity instead of the envelope breaks every RealWorld client (see `LESSONS.md`).

text:
**Refined prompt:** Diagnose whether the always-empty favorite heart is a frontend or backend defect in this NestJS RealWorld API, name the root cause at file:line, fix it at its single source rather than per call site, and state the blast radius, verification, and whether stored data is already wrong. · Assumptions: this repo is backend-only (no UI code exists here), so "frontend" means any standard RealWorld client reading `article.favorited`; I am answering with a diagnosis and a concrete fix plan, not editing files yet.

## Backend. The API never emits `favorited` at all.

### Root cause

`src/article/article.interface.ts:25` — the envelope is typed against the ORM entity:

```ts
export interface ArticleRO {
  article: ArticleEntity;
}
```

`ArticleEntity` (`src/article/article.entity.ts:6-46`) has **no `favorited` property**. Every handler returns that entity raw — `article.service.ts:98` (`return {article}`), `:63`, `:93`, `:144`, `:162` — so the serialized JSON has no `favorited` key. The client does `!!article.favorited` → `!!undefined` → `false` → empty heart, unconditionally, for every article and every user.

The declaration that *looks* like it covers this is dead code:

```ts
// src/article/article.interface.ts:7-18
interface ArticleData {
  ...
  favorited?: boolean;      // :15
  favoritesCount?: number;  // :16
}
```

`ArticleData` is not exported and not referenced anywhere (grep over `src/`: only its own declaration). That is *why this ships green* — the spec-correct shape exists as a type, the envelope points at the entity instead, and TypeScript is satisfied either way.

**Why it can't be fixed downstream:** `favorited` is per-viewer state. It cannot be a column on `article`; it's derived from the `user.favorites` join table (`src/user/user.entity.ts:33-35`). The article read path never loads a caller — `GET /articles` and `GET /articles/:slug` aren't in the middleware list at `src/article/article.module.ts:23-31`, so those handlers have no `userId` to compute it from.

Two more breaks in the same object, same source: `favoriteCount` (`article.entity.ts:45`) is the spec's `favoritesCount`, and `created`/`updated` (`article.entity.ts:24,27`) are `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. The count next to the heart is `undefined` for the same reason.

### The fix — one serializer at the response boundary

1. **Retype the envelope.** `ArticleRO.article: ArticleData`, `ArticlesRO.articles: ArticleData[]`; export `ArticleData` (`article.interface.ts:7,25,29`).
2. **Add one private `toArticleData(article, favoritedIds: Set<number>)` in `ArticleService`** that maps entity → spec shape: rename `favoriteCount`→`favoritesCount`, `created/updated`→`createdAt/updatedAt`, `favorited: favoritedIds.has(article.id)`, and project `author` through `UserData`. Every `return {article}` / `{articles}` goes through it. Do not touch the DB columns — `CURRENT_FOCUS.md` explicitly scopes this to the response boundary.
3. **Make the two public reads optionally authenticated.** You cannot just add them to `forRoutes()`: `auth.middleware.ts:28` throws 401 when there's no header. Needs an `OptionalAuthMiddleware` that calls `next()` on a missing token. Then mirror the existing sibling convention — `ProfileService.findProfile` sets `following` only `if (id)` (`profile.service.ts:43-45`).
4. **Load the ids once per request**, not per article: one query for the caller's favorited article ids → `Set`. `favorite()`/`unFavorite()` already hold the userId and can pass `true`/`false` directly.

### Blast radius

- All 9 `ArticleController` handlers returning `ArticleRO`/`ArticlesRO`.
- Step 1 will **break the build** at `article.service.ts:170` — `create()` is declared `Promise<ArticleEntity>` and returns a bare entity, not the envelope. That's LESSONS.md #57 resurfacing; the compiler catching it is the point.
- Projecting `author` through `UserData` incidentally closes a leak: `findAll` does `leftJoinAndSelect('article.author', 'author')` (`article.service.ts:30`) and returns the entity raw, so **the author's argon2 password hash is currently in every `GET /articles` response** (`user.entity.ts:25-26`; `UserData` at `user.interface.ts:1-7` has no `password`).
- `?favorited=` filtering stays broken independently — `article.service.ts:46` compares `article.authorId IN (:ids)` against *article* ids. Different bug, same feature; fix it in the same pass or it'll look like the serializer failed.

### Is existing data already wrong?

**Probably there is no data.** `article.service.ts:133` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and `:135` immediately reads `user.favorites.findIndex(...)` — but `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany` (`user.entity.ts:33-35`, no `eager: true`, no `relations:` on the call), so it's `undefined` → `TypeError` → 500 on `POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. If that has always been the case, nothing was ever written to the join table and the heart will *still* be empty after the serializer lands. Fix `:133` to `findOne(id, { relations: ['favorites'] })` first, then verify.

The `article.favoriteCount` counter (`article.entity.ts:44-45`) is a denormalized column mutated at `:138`/`:156` with no transaction around the two saves — treat it as untrusted and recount from the join table if any rows exist.

### How to verify

```powershell
# 0. confirm favoriting works at all (expect 500 today)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/articles/<slug>/favorite -H "Authorization: Token $tok"

# 1. as the favoriting user — favorited must be true, favoritesCount a number
curl http://localhost:3000/api/articles/<slug> -H "Authorization: Token $tok"

# 2. same article, no token — favorited false, still 200 (not 401)
curl http://localhost:3000/api/articles/<slug>

# 3. as a different user — favorited false
# 4. the list path too, not just findOne
curl http://localhost:3000/api/articles -H "Authorization: Token $tok"
```

Diff each response against the spec's article object — per LESSONS.md, against the spec, not against what one client happens to read. Assert the absence of `favoriteCount`, `created`, `updated`, and `author.password`.

Want me to implement this? The optional-auth middleware is the one design decision worth confirming first — it's a new file, and the alternative (letting `AuthMiddleware` take a flag) changes behavior for every module that uses it.
